newsitem.title: USA: Brunswick cost cuts, marketing helped Q3.
newsitem.headline: Brunswick cost cuts, marketing helped Q3.

text.p: Recreation equipment maker Brunswick Corp said Monday that its cost-reduction efforts and strong marketing led to higher net earnings and operating margins in the third quarter.
The company's marine segment, for example, reported strong growth despite flatness in the overall market.

"Improved cost management at our Mercury marine engine business led to significant operating margin improvement on a modest sales gain," Peter Larson, chairman and chief executive of Brunswick, said in a statement.
"In addition, enhanced marketing in our core businesses and an improved product mix resulted in excellent growth in boat sales and operating margins," he said.
Marine segment sales were up nine percent to $566.1 million from $517.6 million a year earlier, and operating earnings rose 19 percent to $65 million from $54.7 million.
The recreation segment reported sales of $197.5 million, up 12 percent from $177 million, and operating earnings up 22 percent to $12.6 million from $10.3 million.

Brunswick said its bowling and billiards operations reported higher operating earnings despite a sales decline. The rise resulted from stringent cost controls and stronger sales of higher-margin bowling consumer products, as well as divesture of businesses operating at a loss last year.
Results in the company's fishing tackle operation were hurt by retail inventory adjustments, Brunswick said.
